clue.text: Paris in tatters: end of mortal coil

indicators.note: something in tatters is torn apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of mortal

explanation.surface: A grim French scene: Paris in ruins as someone shuffles off this mortal coil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mortal coil' borrows Hamlet's phrase for life, tempting a reading about death; coil alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A coil is a winding series of loops, the same shape as a spiral.

clue.text: County part of Wales initially? Yes, not English!

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation for English is removed
initially points to the first letter of each word

parts.note: first letters of part, of and Wales
yes without its E

explanation.surface: A query whether a county is part of Wales, answered yes, it isn't English.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true: Powys is a large county in mid-Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Powys is one of the principal areas of Wales, a county in the middle of the country.

clue.text: Change back chain

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A request to swap the bicycle chain at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange is to put things in a new order, a way of altering them.

clue.text: Smallest number oft departing English port

definitions.note: adjectival phrase: lowest, as in the lowest number

indicators.note: something departing leaves, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: Lowestoft is a port in Suffolk, eastern England
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: The fewest ships often departing an English port.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowest means least in amount or value, as the minimum figure in a list.

clue.text: Interval: time one's wasted

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or wrecked, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A complaint about an interval, such as at the theatre, being a waste of one's time.
explanation.walkthrough: Interval reads as a break in a show; here it is the musical sense, the gap between two notes.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a semitone is the smallest interval in Western scales, half a whole tone.

clue.text: Woman expecting to help another couple?

definitions.text: Woman expecting to help another couple?

parts.note: surface: a woman who anticipates being of assistance
cryptic: a pregnant woman carrying a baby on behalf of other parents

explanation.walkthrough: Expecting reads as anticipating, but it means pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: She carries and delivers a child for a couple who cannot have one themselves.

clue.text: Simplest novel badly written

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A judgement on a very simple novel that is poorly written.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a book; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A misspelt word has wrong letters, so it has been written incorrectly.

clue.text: Principle that may come up just the same?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a firmly held belief

definitions.text: that may come up just the same
definitions.meaning: second meaning, cryptic: a word that reads identically when this down light is read upwards

explanation.surface: A principle that might reappear unchanged in debate.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'come up' means read from bottom to top; the second half describes a word that is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a doctrine or belief held as true, which is a guiding principle.

clue.text: Wild maiden not selected

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wild young woman who was not picked.
explanation.definitionFit: To be nominated is to be put forward or chosen for a role, so picked.

clue.text: Damage in weapons — are those offensive?

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the first word goes within the second

parts.note: swords are bladed weapons
wear is damage caused by use

explanation.surface: A question whether damaged weapons are the offensive kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Offensive weapons is a legal phrase, which pulls the reader toward arms; the offence here is to the ear, not the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Swearwords are the rude, offensive terms of the language, so they are those words that offend.

clue.text: Title not applicable with subject of autobiography?

parts.note: N/A is the abbreviation for not applicable
an autobiography is about the writer, me

explanation.surface: A form asks for a title, marked not applicable, alongside notes on an autobiography's subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is what something is called, so it serves as its designation or label.

clue.text: Teas oddly unavailable, push zero for coffee

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are not available, so only the even ones remain

parts.note: second and fourth letters of Teas
to press is to push
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: A café machine has run out of tea, so you push the zero button for coffee instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is a strong Italian coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Number boarding vessel, strong

indicators.note: a passenger boarding a ship goes inside it, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: a pot is a cooking vessel
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A number of passengers boarding a strong ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessel suggests a ship to board; it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Potent means powerful or having great force, as a potent drink is a strong one.

clue.text: Revolution goes quickly backwards

indicators.note: going backwards means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to nip is to go somewhere quickly

explanation.surface: A political revolution that rapidly goes into reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is one turn of something rotating, which is a revolution in the mechanical sense.

clue.text: Say something perhaps before carriage empties

parts.note: something is an example of a part of speech that stands in for a noun

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of carriage

explanation.surface: An announcement made before a train carriage empties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks something as one example of the class of words like it, he and it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to utter or declare, and so to say something aloud formally.

clue.text: Imbibing last of alcohol, tea and cola sadly set aside

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the other letters take this one inside
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters end up in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of alcohol
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sadly sets aside tea and cola to drink alcohol instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate is to assign or earmark something for a purpose, which means setting it aside.

clue.text: Copper racket unlikely to break?

parts.note: a con is a swindle or racket
something stable is steady and secure

explanation.surface: A sturdy copper tennis racket that won't snap.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is the lowest-ranked police officer in Britain, a copper in slang.

clue.text: Actual ban legit, ludicrously

indicators.note: ludicrously means absurdly, so the letters come out in a crazy order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A real ban that is, absurdly, legitimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangible means real enough to touch, so concrete or genuine rather than imagined.

clue.text: News reports finished in jail

indicators.note: being in somewhere means being enclosed by it

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement
something over has finished

explanation.surface: Headlines report on someone who has finished up in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the reporting given to an event by the media, the body of news reports about it.

clue.text: Not one detective gestures in agreement

parts.note: no means not one, as in no people
DS is a Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: A lone detective who refuses to agree while the others signal assent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nods are bowings of the head, the common signal of yes or approval.

clue.text: Slow to collect a shed

indicators.note: collecting something means taking it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: lento is the musical direction for slow
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone slow to pick up a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple outbuilding propped against a wall, a type of shed.

clue.text: Making holes like watching paint dry?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: tedious, as in the idiom for the dullest pastime

explanation.walkthrough: The decorating surface links drilling and paint, but the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the present participle of the verb for drilling and also an adjective meaning dull or tedious.

clue.text: Hidden pub, 'The Queen'

parts.note: an inn is a pub
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A secret pub named The Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner means inside or private, so concealed from the outside world.

clue.text: Up-end open container

parts.note: overt means open, not concealed
an urn is a container, for ashes or tea

explanation.surface: An instruction to tip over an open container.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn is to turn something upside down, the same as tipping it on its end.

clue.text: Country in Peru rallying

indicators.note: in tells the solver the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: last letters of Peru and the start of rallying

explanation.surface: A nation in Peru, rallying for a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Country looks like a nation next to Peru; it is the adjective, as in country life.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes the countryside rather than the town, as in country living.

clue.text: A denial requiring translation soon

parts.note: taken as written
non is French for no, a denial that needs translating

explanation.surface: A refusal that has to be translated soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Requiring translation' tells the solver the denial is in a foreign language, here French.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word meaning shortly or in a little while.

clue.text: Where landlord might stand in prison

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pub landlord serves from the far side of the counters
second meaning: locked up, as in a cell

explanation.walkthrough: Landlord here is the British keeper of a pub, not someone who rents out property.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally places someone at the back of a pub counter and idiomatically means jailed.

clue.text: I agree at this point to speak repeatedly?

indicators.note: repeatedly means the same piece is used again, placed side by side twice
speaking means saying words out loud, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: here means at this point, said twice

explanation.surface: Someone agrees, saying it is their turn to speak, and then repeats themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The cry is used in Parliament and meetings to back a speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a traditional British way of showing approval of what a speaker has just said.

clue.text: Too old really, Labour leader admitted

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: something admitted is let in, so it goes inside the other word

parts.note: very and really both intensify

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A complaint that the Labour leader is really too old for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Overly means excessively, the same as too in a phrase such as too keen.
